messages:
rahul: Heads-up — after yesterday's rollout I see an intermittent perf regression on medium-length chat workloads when prefix cache hit rate increases (~>60%). p95 token latency jumped from 92ms -> 170ms on g5.

maria: hmm, that's worrying. Any change in kernel selection logs or just queueing?

rahul: Profiling shows more frequent kernel fallback to generic attention for long KV paths. Also batching changed shape: many requests were small (cache-hit) but we were packing them with cold requests and hitting token budget limits, causing early flushes.

ben: Can you paste the kernel selection excerpt and the batcher config?

rahul: Sure — kernel trace snippet: 
```
[2026-03-16T18:42:10Z] model_x: selected kernel=attn_opt_v2 for seq=32, kv_len=0
[2026-03-16T18:42:11Z] model_x: fallback kernel=attn_generic for seq=192, kv_len=1024
[2026-03-16T18:42:11Z] model_x: selected kernel=attn_opt_v1 for seq=64, kv_len=512
```

rahul: Batcher config used in this shard: 
```
{\n  token_budget_target: 4096,\n  max_batch_tokens: 8192,\n  queue_policy: FIFO,\n  prefer_large_batches: true\n}
```

alice: So when KV cache hits are high you get lots of short token sequences (only new tokens), but we still counted kv_len in kernel heuristics? That mismatch would force kernel that expects long kv to run generically.

dan: Also if cache-hit requests are packed with cold requests, the effective sequence-length variance increases which hurts the optimized kernels that rely on tight shape assumptions.

maria: We should make batcher cache-hit-aware: treat cache-hit requests as lower token-cost (or a different token budget class), and prefer packing cache-hits together so they can use optimized kernels.

ben: Proposed quick experiment: 3-arm A/B on a shard —
- Arm A: baseline (current)
- Arm B: token_budget_target scaled by (1 + 0.5 * cache_hit_rate)
- Arm C: separate queue for cache-hit requests with priority=high, pack-only-within-queue true

rahul: Ran Arm B for 2 hours on canary: p95 improved from 170ms -> 100ms for high cache-hit traffic, throughput unchanged. CPU/GPU utilization shifted slightly (more kernel-optimal paths).

alice: Nice. Any regressions on low cache-hit traffic?

rahul: Minimal — Arm B slightly increased latency for fully cold long-context requests (+8ms p95) but still within SLO. Arm C looked even better on p95 but introduced starvation risk for cold requests under 95th-percentile load.

maria: We should add a hybrid queue-policy: cache-hit queue with aggressive packing and token budget multiplier, plus an escape window for cold requests so they can't be starved >50ms beyond baseline.

ben: Agree. Also update kernel-selection heuristics to consider effective_new_tokens and cached_kv_size separately: current heuristic uses total_seq = kv_len + new_tokens which over-penalizes cache-hits.

rahul: Pseudocode we used for packing tweak:
```
if request.cache_hit_fraction >= 0.6:
  budget = base_budget * (1 + 0.5 * request.cache_hit_fraction)
  queue = CACHE_HIT_QUEUE
else:
  budget = base_budget
  queue = NORMAL_QUEUE
```

dan: We should add a perf test in CI that simulates 70% cache hits with mixed new token lengths and assert kernel selection ratio (opt_v* / generic) > 0.8 and p95 token latency < 120ms. @ci-bot can we add that?

ci-bot: Job created: perf/cache-hit-batching-sim (queue: nightly-e2e).

maria: I'll draft an RFC with measured numbers, approach, and mitigations (escape window + kernel heuristic change). Good work catching this, @rahul. :tada:

rahul: Thanks team. Next steps: RFC, small canary for Arm C with starvation watch, and CI perf test.

alice: Can someone add a note in the rollout playbook about monitoring kernel fallback ratio (metric: runtime.kernel.fallback_rate) and cache-hit packing success?

ben: I'll add the dashboard tiles.

rahul: Copy that — I'll open the PR for the batcher change today.
